about.title: About — Secufile
about.description: How Secufile keeps your files safe (encryption, password protection, automatic deletion), and about its operator, the non-profit PAPS.
about.body:
About this service

Secufile is a free file-transfer service run by the certified non-profit PAPS. No account is needed.

Why we make this public

At PAPS, we need to exchange evidence images and sensitive data securely with lawyers, law-enforcement agencies and others.

With ordinary email, even when the connection is encrypted, copies of a file can remain on mail services and at the destination. And if you send it to the wrong address, it is hard to fully undo afterwards.

These problems are not unique to support work. Anyone can face a situation where they want to send a file safely (personal information, contracts, photos, evidence) that they would rather others not see.

So we have opened the system PAPS actually needed in its support work as a free service anyone can use.

How files are protected

Each uploaded file is encrypted and stored with AES-256-GCM, using a random data-encryption key generated per file.

AES was adopted as the U.S. government standard cipher and is used worldwide to protect classified information, including in defense. AES-256 has been scrutinized for its security by cryptographers around the world over many years.

AES-256-GCM not only makes the contents unreadable, but can also verify that stored data has not been tampered with or corrupted. Secufile splits each file into fixed-size blocks and encrypts and authenticates each one.

What is Argon2id

Argon2id is a key derivation function designed to turn a password into a secure encryption key.

A password a person sets is usually shorter than a fully random key and may use dictionary words or predictable patterns. Using a password directly as an encryption key is therefore not safe.

Also, ordinary hash functions compute very fast, so an attacker can try a huge number of password candidates in a short time.

Argon2id deliberately uses not only a fixed amount of time per computation but also a large amount of memory. An attack that tries millions or billions of candidates at once with GPUs or dedicated hardware therefore needs a large amount of memory and computing resources.

For a user entering the correct password it is a one-time operation, but for an attacker trying countless candidates the cost adds up with each attempt. This greatly increases the time and money needed for a brute-force attack.

Argon2id combines the properties of Argon2i, which guards against information leakage while deriving a key, and Argon2d, which emphasizes resistance to brute-force attacks. It is recommended in the international technical document RFC 9106 and by OWASP.

By adopting Argon2id, Secufile increases resistance to password cracking compared with deriving an encryption key directly and simply from the password.

We do not store the password itself

What is stored on the server is the encrypted file and the encrypted data-encryption key. The password the user entered is stored nowhere on the server.

File names are encrypted too, so the contents cannot be guessed from a stored file name.

Therefore, even if only the data stored on the server were obtained, reading the contents without the password is extremely difficult.

Important: if you lose the password, the file cannot be recovered. Not even PAPS can check the password or recover the file. Using an easily guessed password (a short string or a common word) lowers security. Please use the auto-generated password, or set one that is long enough and hard to guess.

Communication is encrypted too

All communication between the browser and the Secufile server is encrypted with TLS (HTTPS).

This reduces the risk of a third party eavesdropping on the contents during upload or download.

Files are deleted automatically

A file is deleted automatically when either of the following is reached:

  • the retention period set by the sender has passed
  • the configured download limit has been reached

If the sender allows it, the recipient can also delete the file on the spot after downloading.

By not storing files longer than necessary, we reduce the risk of information lingering.

Information we record

To respond to rights infringement and to lawful requests for sender-information disclosure, we record and retain the uploader IP address.

If illegal information, or information that infringes the rights of others, is posted, we may disclose information to the relevant authorities or rights holders, in accordance with the law and the terms of use.

Secufile may not be used for the purpose of sharing illegal or harmful information.

Large files are supported

Files are uploaded in small parts.

If the connection drops partway, it resumes automatically from where it stopped once the connection recovers. Even on an unstable connection such as mobile, you do not have to resend from the beginning.

Downloads can also be resumed from where they were interrupted.

About the operator

Secufile is developed and operated by PAPS (a certified non-profit organization), which supports victims of sexual exploitation and digital sexual violence.

PAPS provides counseling support, help removing sexual images and videos, street outreach, safe spaces and accommodation for young women, and technology development to detect harm early.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy — Secufile
privacy.description: How Secufile handles personal and access information.
privacy.body:
Privacy Policy

Information we collect

  • Uploaded files (stored only in encrypted form)
  • File names (stored only in encrypted form)
  • File size, count, upload time, expiry, and download count
  • The uploader's IP address (for responding to sender-information disclosure requests and to misuse)
  • Access logs (for error investigation and abuse detection)

Information we do not collect

  • Registration details such as name or email (there is no account system)
  • The plaintext of file contents or file names
  • The share password

Advertising

Some pages of this service use Google's advertising service (Google AdSense). Google may use cookies to serve ads, which may show ads based on a user's prior visits. You can turn off the cookies used for advertising from Google's Advertising policy.

Analytics

Some pages use Google Analytics (GA4, measurement ID G-4PJ2LXFFR2) to understand usage. Google Analytics uses cookies to collect traffic data; the data is anonymous and does not identify individuals. It is not loaded on download or pickup pages, or any page whose URL contains a share link. You can refuse collection by disabling cookies in your browser or installing Google's opt-out add-on. See Google's policy for details.

Disclosure to third parties

Except where required by law or under a legitimate procedure such as a sender-information disclosure request, we do not provide the collected information to third parties. If illegal or harmful material is posted, we may disclose necessary information to the relevant authorities or rights holders.

Retention

Files and their associated metadata are deleted when the expiry is reached or the download limit is hit. Access logs and IP addresses are retained only for as long as is necessary for operation and response.

Contact

For inquiries about this policy, please contact PAPS.
terms.title: Terms of Service — Secufile
terms.description: The terms of service for Secufile, including prohibited uses and disclaimers.
terms.body:
Terms of Service

1. The service

Secufile is a file-transfer service provided free of charge by PAPS (a certified non-profit organization). The service may change or be discontinued without notice.

2. Prohibited uses

  • Sending content that violates the law or promotes illegal acts
  • Sending content that infringes the copyright, likeness rights, privacy, or other rights of others
  • Sending sexual images or videos taken or obtained without the subject's consent
  • Sending malware or other harmful programs
  • Interfering with the operation of the service

3. Disclaimer

We make no guarantee as to the storage, availability, or integrity of files. Even before the expiry, a file may become unavailable due to a failure, a legal request, or a violation of these terms.

By the design of the encryption, if the share password is lost there is no way to recover the file. Not even PAPS can recover it.

4. Responding to infringement

If content that infringes rights is found, we may delete the file without prior notice and provide information to the relevant authorities as needed. Please submit reports from Report infringement.

faq.title: FAQ | Secufile
faq.description: Frequently asked questions about Secufile: free large-file transfer, encryption and security, retention, a safe alternative to password-protected ZIP (PPAP), and sending from a phone.
faq.lead: Answers about free large-file transfer, encryption, retention, and replacing PPAP.
faq.a1: Yes. Secufile is completely free with no sign-up. It is run by the Japanese non-profit PAPS (特定非営利活動法人ぱっぷす).
faq.q2: How large a file can I send?
faq.a2: Up to 10 GB and 100 files per transfer. Choosing a longer retention or more downloads lowers the limit a little.
faq.q3: Is it secure? Are files encrypted?
faq.a3: Files are encrypted with a password before they leave your device, so even the server operator cannot read them. The password is never stored, so no third party can recover a lost file.
faq.a4: You can set retention from 1 to 100 days. Files are deleted automatically when they expire or reach the download limit.
faq.q5: Can I use it instead of a password-protected ZIP (PPAP)?
faq.a5: Yes. It encrypts the file itself without making a ZIP, so it is a safer alternative to PPAP. Share the password through a different channel than the link.
faq.q6: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a6: Yes. Pick files or photos straight from your phone's browser and send them. There is no app to install.
faq.q7: Does the recipient need an account?
faq.a7: No. They just open the link and enter the password to download.
faq.q8: Can I delete a file I sent?
faq.a8: Yes. Create a management link when you send, and you alone can check download status and delete the share manually.
guide.title: How to use — send large files free | Secufile
guide.description: How to use Secufile: choose files or a message, encrypt with a password, and get a share link. Works for large files, as a PPAP replacement, and from your phone.
guide.lead: Choose files, upload, and share the link — done in three or four steps.
guide.step1_text: Drag and drop files on the home page, or click to choose. Folders and pasted clipboard images work too. To send text only, pick the Message tab.
guide.step2_text: Open Advanced settings to change retention or the download limit. A password is generated for you. Tick “Create a management link” if you want to track downloads.
guide.step3_name: Upload and get the share link
guide.step3_text: Press Upload; the files are encrypted and uploaded, and a share link, password, and QR code appear.
guide.step4_text: For safety, send the link and password through different channels (for example, the link by email and the password by chat).
guide.body:
When a file is too large to email

Email attachments are often capped at a few to a few dozen MB, so large videos or photo folders won't go through. Secufile sends up to 10 GB per transfer as a single link — the recipient just opens it and downloads.

A safer alternative to password-protected ZIP (PPAP)

Sending a ZIP and then its password over the same channel is weak. Secufile encrypts the file itself before it reaches the server and never stores the password. Share the link and password separately for safer delivery.

Send photos and videos from your phone

Pick photos and videos straight from your phone's browser and upload them. No app and no sign-up — share what you just shot, securely.

Send a secret message

Beyond files, you can send short text — a password or a note — encrypted. Choose the Message tab, type your message, and send.
about.oss_body:
The software that runs this service is published under the MIT license for anyone to read and verify: github.com/paps-jp/securefile

You can confirm how encryption and files are handled from the actual code, not just from our description. Being verifiable by third parties means you do not have to trust the operator unconditionally — transparency itself strengthens security.
